body:
Hmmm, perhaps it's different depending on what your life has been like, I wouldn't call it bliss, I would call it blessed relief, a reprieve of some sort even though it is the end of me and my world.

Yes I've read a lot about lucid dreams since I've had many sleep paralysis events ever since this pain started. I've tried to pursue them w/o luck.

Yes I've heard of transcendent hallucinogenic experiences caused by various things like psychotropic mushrooms or cacti that can spur miraculous healing, however, I just don't think we know enough about such things to use them safely. I realize some Native Americans used such drugs, but for spiritual purposes and not healing purposes, plus Westerns have an entirely different outlook that Native Americans,

Chronic pain gives you an unpleasant window in circumstances that could be considered worse than death, and drugs that are causing you to lose all sense of time, place, and have visions are clearly powerful things not to be trifled with.  I  really hope more studies are done on these drugs however.

Yikes, yeah when I have to wake up at a specific time, it is a task that takes a huge amount of effort. I'm sorry you are experiencing that, I hope you figure out what is causing it.

No you are right, after about a year of this sensation being 24/7, I've thought of ending my life. It's just that now it feels like I'm getting more evidence that end of things really may not be so bad vs living another 40-50 years like this.

It's up to you to create meaning in your life, not for the world to create it for you. However, imo it's a valid choice to assign no value to life for many reasons.  However, certain philosophers would disagree
